cards.title: Why your heart can never cramp into a locked muscle spasm
cards.body: Skeletal muscles can cramp into sustained, painful contractions called tetanus when stimulated repeatedly. Your heart, however, is physiologically incapable of cramping. Cardiac muscle cells possess an extraordinarily long electrical refractory period lasting roughly 250 milliseconds. Because this pause lasts nearly as long as the mechanical contraction itself, the heart muscle is physically forced to relax and refill with blood between every single beat.

cards.title: Carbon monoxide suffocates cells by binding hemoglobin over 200 times tighter than oxygen
cards.body: Carbon monoxide is lethal because it starves tissues of oxygen without triggering any sensation of choking. Inhaled carbon monoxide binds to the iron atom in hemoglobin with an affinity roughly 200 to 250 times greater than oxygen. Once locked in place, it forms carboxyhemoglobin, which not only blocks fresh oxygen from hitching a ride but also prevents hemoglobin from releasing the oxygen it already carries.

cards.title: Rapid decompression turns dissolved blood nitrogen into fizzing bubbles
cards.body: While breathing compressed air underwater, ambient pressure forces inert nitrogen gas to dissolve into your blood and fatty tissues. If you ascend toward the surface too quickly, ambient pressure drops precipitously, causing that dissolved nitrogen to rapidly boil out of solution as microscopic gas bubbles. These bubbles lodge in capillaries, tear blood vessel linings, and pinch nerves, producing the agonizing condition called decompression sickness.

cards.title: The longest single cells in your body stretch over three feet
cards.body: While most human cells are microscopic, the motor neurons that control your feet are astonishing biological cables. Their cell bodies reside in your lower spinal cord, but a single continuous axon fiber stretches all the way down your leg to muscles in your toes, measuring over three feet long in adults. To keep this distant terminal alive, the cell body continuously shuttles vital proteins down its microscopic highway.

cards.title: The blood-testis barrier protects developing sperm from your own immune system
cards.body: Because sperm production begins at puberty—long after your immune system has cataloged your body's native tissues—developing sperm express novel surface proteins your white blood cells have never seen before. To prevent autoimmune destruction, specialized Sertoli cells construct the blood-testis barrier using ultra-tight cellular junctions. This barrier physically isolates developing sperm from blood and lymph, preventing your immune system from manufacturing antibodies against its own reproductive cells.

quizzes.question: What prevents human cardiac muscle from locking into a sustained cramp or spasm (tetanus)?
options: A long electrical refractory period that forces relaxation between beats
The complete absence of calcium inside heart cells
Continuous inhibitory signals sent from the optic nerve
The inability of heart tissue to conduct action potentials
quizzes.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells have a prolonged refractory period of ~250 ms, ensuring the heart relaxes and refills with blood before it can contract again.

quizzes.question: Why is carbon monoxide exceptionally effective at starving bodily tissues of oxygen?
options: It binds to hemoglobin over 200 times more tightly than oxygen
It instantly destroys red blood cells upon contact in the lungs
It paralyzes the diaphragm muscle so you cannot inhale
It converts dissolved oxygen in blood into carbon dioxide
quizzes.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin with an affinity 200 to 250 times greater than oxygen, locking onto binding sites and altering hemoglobin's release shape.

quizzes.question: What physically causes decompression sickness (the bends) in scuba divers?
options: Dissolved nitrogen gas coming out of solution as bubbles during a fast ascent
Severe chemical burns caused by breathing compressed oxygen
Sudden electrolyte loss caused by immersion in cold seawater
Rapid collapse of lung alveoli due to high external pressure
quizzes.explanation: Ascending too quickly drops ambient pressure rapidly, causing dissolved nitrogen in blood and tissues to form bubbles that obstruct circulation.

quizzes.question: Where are the longest single nerve fibers (axons) in the human body located?
options: Running from the lower spinal cord all the way down to the toes
Extending from the brainstem down into the small intestine
Connecting the retina directly to the frontal cortex
Stretching from the collarbone across the chest to the ribs
quizzes.explanation: Motor axons in the sciatic nerve path originate in the lower spinal cord and travel continuously down the entire leg into the foot.

quizzes.question: Why does the human body maintain a blood-testis barrier around developing sperm?
options: To prevent immune cells from attacking novel proteins on sperm cells
To keep testosterone from escaping into general blood circulation
To stop red blood cells from consuming all available testicular glucose
To block atmospheric oxygen from entering reproductive tissue
quizzes.explanation: Because sperm cells develop after puberty, the immune system would treat their novel proteins as foreign invaders without this protective barrier.

guesses.prompt: How many times more tightly does carbon monoxide bind to human hemoglobin compared to oxygen?
guesses.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin roughly 200 to 250 times more tightly than oxygen, aggressively outcompeting it.

guesses.prompt: In inches, roughly how long is the longest single nerve cell in an adult human body?
guesses.explanation: Motor neurons running from the base of the spinal cord to the toes can measure 3 feet (36 inches) or more in length.

misconceptions.claim: Your heart muscle can cramp into a continuous spasm just like your calves or thighs.
misconceptions.explanation: The heart has an unusually long refractory period that prevents tetanus, forcing muscle fibers to fully relax between beats.

misconceptions.claim: Divers get the bends because oxygen in their bloodstream turns into gas bubbles.
misconceptions.explanation: Decompression sickness is caused by inert nitrogen gas coming out of solution when external pressure drops, not oxygen.
